The operational process of a mass spectrometer shown on the figure below is divided into
© Ionisation: The atom is ionised by knocking one or more electrons off to give a
positive ion. Mass spectrometers always work with positive ions.
Acceleration: The ions are accelerated so that they all have the same kinetic
© Deflection: The ions are deflected by a magnetic field according to their masses.
The lighter they are, the more they are deflected. The amount of deflection also
depends on the number of positive charges on the ion. The more the ion is
charged, the more it gets deflected.
© Detection: The beam of ions passing through the machine is detected electrically.
